v2_leakage_risks.description: Transformation type or details could be inferred from execution trace content (stdout/stderr). If a semantic transformation (such as SP-1 variable renaming) changes printed exception messages, traceback structures, or custom debug prints, or if class/function names are logged during dynamic execution, the evaluation model can infer the transformation type.
v2_leakage_risks.mitigation: Strictly sanitize all stdout, stderr, and trace output. Standardize trace captures to structured return values or serialized program state, stripping out tracebacks, exception details referencing variable names, or internal class/function names.

v2_leakage_risks.description: Filename/path names could appear in stack traces, system errors, or __file__ variables. If temporary execution files use names like 'tmp_SP1_program.py' or if programs print their own names dynamically, the pair identity or transformation class is directly leaked.
v2_leakage_risks.mitigation: Execute programs in a sandboxed environment where __file__ is mocked or inaccessible. Preprocess all stack traces and replace specific file paths, temporary names, and line references with generalized placeholders.

v2_leakage_risks.description: Semantic transformations (SP) change program structure or add/remove helper logic which can affect execution duration. If timing systematically differs between SP and SC transformations, a model could exploit this. However, execution noise usually overwhelms small structural timing differences.
v2_leakage_risks.mitigation: Excluding execution time/durations from the trace data made visible to the evaluation models, and enforcing a strict timeout cap for all execution runs.

v2_leakage_risks.description: Use of system clock calls (time.time, time.monotonic, datetime.now), sleep delays (time.sleep), memory address queries (id()), or concurrent threads leads to non-deterministic program state and output variation between runs. This results in false mismatches or false equivalents in dynamic verification.
v2_leakage_risks.mitigation: Mock/patch time.time, time.monotonic, and id() during dynamic execution, and replace real sleeps with virtual clock updates. Exclude or restrict multi-threaded base programs from direct dynamic trace comparison unless thread execution is strictly synchronized/serialized.

v2_leakage_risks.description: If two programs exhibit identical behavior on a limited set of fixed inputs but differ on other input paths, the dynamic execution suite will incorrectly label them as equivalent (false equivalents) due to sparse input coverage.
v2_leakage_risks.mitigation: Utilize diverse and comprehensive input generation including automatically generated boundary values, edge cases, and random-seeded fuzzing inputs to maximize code path coverage.
